description: Lifecycle interaction obligations (#4099): t=2 pairs of OP, SRC, PRIM, SCOPE, LOCK, DEPLOYED, GATE, TGT, NET and the modifiers, the exception factors crossed with the factors they refine, and the named triples T1-T5, after the refusal, definition and partial-equivalence rules of tests/lifecycle/generator/rules.py. required ids are credited by oracles.check_obligation in their witness (a covering row, or a machine spine whose credited_by ids imply the cell); known-failing ids name the strict known cell's tracking issue; baseline ids name the lane and issue that must discharge them. Regenerate with `python -m tests.lifecycle.generator`; `--check` fails on drift.

E1.text: hosts are equivalent except lock identity (HOSTID)

E2.text: targets are equivalent except MCP ownership (MCPOWN)

E3.text: file primitives are equivalent except compile-staging routing (FILEROUTE)

U-BIN.text: bin/ deploys only for a marketplace plugin installed at user scope with a Claude target that supports skills (plugin_bin_deployable), so bin/ at project scope is unreachable and removed. The package type, not SRC, makes a marketplace plugin, so SRC cells stay. Self-reinstating: the generator hashes the predicate (generator/bin_pin.py); when the hash differs from U_BIN_PIN the cells return as must-cover and --check fails until a reviewed change updates the pin. The closed-world pins of the bin/ writer and unpack live with the gate tables (T3)

U-FIRST-PARTY-MCP.text: an MCP server the project declares in its own apm.yml is first-party: the executables gate governs servers from dependencies and never parks it, so every executable-gate level of an MCP source is one must-cover cell that witnesses it (an org policy dependency deny still applies)

U-MKT.text: marketplace commands act on catalogs, never on deployed primitives: add, list, browse, update, remove and validate read or refresh the catalog cache, and the authoring commands edit the marketplace block; a primitive reaches a project only through install of plugin@marketplace (OP=install, SRC=marketplace-*). Every OP=marketplace x PRIM cell but the org-policy GATE level (U2 no-collapse) maps onto one rule cell witnessed at the allowed and the revoked GATE level (deployed surfaces and the lock byte-identical)

U1.text: a modifier the command does not accept is one refusal cell per command

U10.text: compile renders hook/mcp/lsp only; --validate reads MCP declarations

U11.text: --frozen refuses any declared-target change before it changes anything: a dropped target (#4517) and an added one. A changed TGT with FROZEN maps to one refusal cell, witnessed by the T-6a history scenario

U2.text: the executable gate governs only executable primitives; a plain file next to a revoked executable must survive; an org policy dependency deny removes it

U3.text: edited is defined relative to a receipt; present with unknown provenance has no lock

U4.text: a declared target change without a receipt is reachable; only receipt-backed contraction needs a prior lock

U6.text: pack provenance is the dependencies / marketplace block, not SRC

U7.text: mcp-install acts on the requested server; other primitives keep no-collateral-write

U8.text: the source decides the command: bundle-install is install of a local bundle (install x local-bundle maps to it; no other source can state it); install --mcp takes an MCP registry name or an inline server (--url, or a command after --), never a package source, and an MCP source delivers only MCP; a package registry delivers whole packages. Parsed-then-refused shapes are refusal cells, one per message class: marketplace add of a source without a catalog, uninstall of an MCP server (a registry name is not found in apm.yml; an inline name is an MCP server), and a local bundle, which writes no manifest entry (uninstall refuses it; update and prune leave it untouched). A native plugin carries no canvas primitive

U9.text: approve/deny with no prior decision is reachable; --list and --pending are read-only
